alloy.preparation: A35, nominal CoCrFeNi2, classified as HEA by the authors. Commercial-purity materials and in-house refined Ni–Co–Cr master alloys; approximately 8000 g induction melted under inert gas and poured with 50 °C superheat into 75 mm cylindrical graphite mold with nonreactive ceramic wash. Hot-tops band-sawn off and chemistry slice taken. Computationally optimized homogenization heat treatment (numerical schedule not supplied), sidewalls lathe conditioned, bagged in protective stainless-steel foil pouches and preheated for 3 h. A35 hot worked at 900 °C by forging and rolling into approximately 3.7 mm thick strip. Corrosion specimens 15 × 10 × 3 mm machined from strip, with a 3–48 threaded hole in a 10 × 3 mm end; SiC abrasive slurry/lapping removed tool marks. Before electrochemical testing, wet ground to 600-grit SiC finish, degreased with acetone and air dried; tightly screwed to the threaded-rod holder before immersion.
alloy.microstructure: Single FCC phase, fully recrystallized equiaxed grains after forging/rolling, average 40 µm with reported standard deviation 4.8 µm; ASTM grain size 6. Small casting inclusions observed. Figure 3 caption calls the micrographs as-cast, whereas preparation and Section 3.1 explicitly discuss hot-worked/recrystallized specimens.

test_solution.preparation: Nondeaerated solution; initial pH 8.4 before potentiodynamic polarization. No salt recipe or gas-purging procedure supplied.

test_method.procedure_description: Three-electrode glass cell with metal working electrode, calomel reference (SCE) and Pt-sheet counter; Luggin capillary to reduce uncompensated IR drop; Gamry Reference 600+ potentiostat/galvanostat/ZRA. Before each test, held 800 mV more negative than free potential for 2 min, followed by 30 min OCP measurement. Potentiodynamic scan from −0.25 V versus Eoc to 1.6 V versus Eoc. Separate cyclic measurements reverse at 1.5 V versus Eoc, and EIS is a separate passive-film assessment.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Authors’ breakdown potential Ebre associated with passive-film breakdown and pitting; for A35, explicitly the nucleation/growth/repassivation of metastable pits. No universal numerical current threshold is stated. Large hysteresis in the separate cyclic tests and SEM support pitting susceptibility for A35 and SS316.

experiments.result_note: The paper associates Ebre with metastable pit initiation in A35. Text, Table 2 and conclusions repeat this outcome. The source also prints 0.56 V versus SHE for the same result; its original alternative reading is retained without a conversion performed here. After potentiodynamic polarization the A35 solution pH was reported as 10.9; the structured pH field retains the initial value 8.4. No pH calculation is performed. Table 1 chemistry retains both wt.% and ppm as printed, without unit conversion or balance calculation. The Figure 6 caption uses the word saturated, while the methods consistently specify a nondeaerated 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution; no saturation concentration is inferred.

alloy.preparation: Commercial stainless-steel SS316 comparison, called 316L in the abstract; the source also prints UNS 31600. Detailed manufacturing/heat treatment is not supplied for this comparator. Bare corrosion specimens machined and fitted to the threaded-rod holder for electrochemical tests; the experimental-HEA melting/homogenization/hot-working treatment is not assigned to SS316. Before electrochemical testing, wet ground to 600-grit SiC finish, degreased with acetone and air dried; tightly screwed to the threaded-rod holder before immersion.
alloy.microstructure: Austenitic stainless-steel comparator, ASTM grain size 7 reported in Table 1.
